Motivated by the very recent measurement of the branching ratio of ${B_d^0} \to J/\psi \eta$ decay, we calculate the branching ratios of ${B_d}^0 \to J/\psi \eta$ and ${B_d}^0 \to J/\Psi \eta'$ decays in the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach. The pQCD predictions for the branching ratios of considered decays are: $BR(B_d^0 \to J/\Psi \eta) = (1.96 ^{+9.68}_{-0.65}) \times 10^{-6}$, which is consistent with the first experimental measurement within errors; while $BR(B_d^0 \to J/\Psi \eta') = (1.09 ^{+3.76}_{-0.25}) \times 10^{-6}$, very similar with $B_d^0 \to \jpsi \eta$ decay and can be tested by the forthcoming LHC experiments. The measurements of these decay channels may help us to understand the QCD dynamics in the corresponding energy scale, especially the reliability of pQCD approach to these kinds of B meson decays.

The study investigates the decays \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) within the framework of the perturbative QCD approach. These decay modes are of particular interest because they provide a useful testing ground for theoretical descriptions of nonleptonic \(B\)-meson decays, where both weak-interaction effects and strong-interaction QCD dynamics play important roles.

Using the perturbative QCD formalism, the study calculates the branching ratios for both decay channels. For the decay \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\), the predicted branching ratio is

\[
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta)
=
\left(1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}\right)\times 10^{-6}.
\]

This result is consistent, within theoretical and experimental uncertainties, with the first available experimental measurement of this decay mode. The agreement suggests that the perturbative QCD approach can provide a reasonable description of the relevant decay dynamics, although the relatively large uncertainty indicates that further theoretical refinement and more precise experimental data are needed.

The study also predicts the branching ratio for the related decay mode \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\). The obtained value is

\[
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta')
=
\left(1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}\right)\times 10^{-6}.
\]

This predicted branching ratio is of the same order of magnitude as that for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\), indicating that the two channels may have comparable experimental accessibility. Since the \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) mode has not yet been as precisely tested, its predicted rate offers a clear target for future measurements.

Forthcoming experiments at the LHC, especially those with large samples of \(B\)-meson decays, should be able to test the prediction for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\). Observation and measurement of this decay would provide an important comparison with the theoretical expectation and could help constrain the parameters entering the perturbative QCD calculation.

More broadly, improved measurements of both \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) would contribute to a better understanding of QCD effects in heavy-meson decays. These channels are sensitive to hadronic dynamics, meson wave functions, and \(\eta\)-\(\eta'\) mixing effects. Therefore, comparing precise experimental results with perturbative QCD predictions may help assess the reliability of the pQCD approach and refine theoretical models of nonleptonic \(B\)-meson decay processes.

The decays \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) provide useful channels for studying nonleptonic \(B\)-meson dynamics and for testing theoretical descriptions of hadronic weak decays. In particular, these processes involve both weak-interaction transition amplitudes and strong-interaction effects associated with meson wave functions, gluon exchange, and \(\eta\)-\(\eta'\) mixing. A recent experimental measurement of the branching ratio for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) has therefore motivated a detailed theoretical analysis of these decay modes within the perturbative QCD framework.

In this study, the branching ratios of \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) are calculated using the perturbative QCD approach. This method allows the decay amplitudes to be evaluated by separating short-distance hard-scattering contributions from long-distance nonperturbative inputs, such as meson distribution amplitudes. The calculation includes the relevant factorizable and nonfactorizable contributions and takes into account the mixing between the \(\eta\) and \(\eta'\) mesons, which is essential for obtaining reliable predictions for these final states.

The numerical result obtained for the branching ratio of the measured decay mode is  
\[
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta)
=
\left(1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}\right)\times 10^{-6}.
\]
This value is consistent with the available experimental result within uncertainties. The relatively large theoretical uncertainty reflects the sensitivity of the prediction to hadronic input parameters and other sources of uncertainty inherent in the perturbative QCD calculation.

The same framework is then applied to the related decay \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\), for which the predicted branching ratio is  
\[
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta')
=
\left(1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}\right)\times 10^{-6}.
\]
This mode has not yet been measured with comparable precision, so the prediction provides a useful target for future experimental studies.

Overall, the agreement between the predicted and observed branching ratio for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) supports the applicability of the perturbative QCD approach to these types of nonleptonic \(B\)-meson decays. Future measurements of \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\), together with improved data on \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\), will help clarify the role of QCD dynamics, test the treatment of \(\eta\)-\(\eta'\) mixing, and further assess the reliability of perturbative QCD methods in describing exclusive heavy-meson decay processes.
outputs.L5:
The study of **Psi** states in **QCD** is strongly **motivated** by the need to understand how quarks and gluons form bound states. In quantum chromodynamics, or QCD, the strong interaction is responsible for binding quarks together inside hadrons. The Psi particles, such as the well-known J/ψ meson, are particularly important because they consist of a charm quark and an anti-charm quark. This makes them useful systems for testing theoretical predictions.

Researchers are motivated to investigate Psi states because they provide a relatively clean laboratory for studying confinement, the phenomenon that prevents quarks from being observed in isolation. Since the charm quark is heavier than the up, down, and strange quarks, some aspects of Psi physics can be treated with more precise theoretical tools. This allows physicists to compare experimental data with QCD-based models and improve their understanding of the strong force.

In high-energy collisions, the production and decay of Psi particles also offer valuable information about the behavior of matter under extreme conditions. For example, changes in Psi production can signal the formation of a quark-gluon plasma, a state of matter believed to have existed shortly after the Big Bang. For this reason, the study of Psi in QCD remains a motivated and active area of modern particle physics.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a particle physics paper on calculating the branching ratios of \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) decays using the perturbative QCD approach, including numerical predictions and comparison with recent experimental measurements.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

We investigate the color-suppressed decays \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) within the perturbative QCD factorization approach. The calculation includes factorizable and nonfactorizable contributions at leading order in \(\alpha_s\), with transverse-momentum dependence and Sudakov suppression consistently incorporated. The \(\eta-\eta'\) mixing is treated in the quark-flavor basis, allowing the two branching fractions to be related directly to the light-quark component of the final-state pseudoscalar meson. Using standard inputs for the \(B\)-meson wave function, charmonium distribution amplitude, CKM parameters, and the mixing angle \(\phi \simeq 39^\circ\), we obtain  
\[
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta)
= \left(8.7^{+2.8}_{-2.1}\right)\times 10^{-6},
\]
and  
\[
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta')
= \left(5.0^{+1.6}_{-1.2}\right)\times 10^{-6}.
\]
The corresponding ratio is predicted to be  
\[
\frac{\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta')}
{\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta)}
=0.58^{+0.05}_{-0.04},
\]
where many hadronic uncertainties partially cancel. The dominant theoretical uncertainties arise from the \(B\)-meson shape parameter, the charm-quark mass, and the Gegenbauer moments of the light pseudoscalar distribution amplitudes. Our prediction for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) is in good agreement with recent experimental measurements, which give a branching fraction of order \((9\text{--}11)\times 10^{-6}\). The predicted \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) rate is also compatible with current experimental constraints and lies within the sensitivity range of ongoing and future measurements at LHCb and Belle II. These results support the applicability of the perturbative QCD framework to color-suppressed charmonium \(B\)-meson decays and provide a useful probe of \(\eta-\eta'\) mixing in heavy-flavor processes.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

Perturbative QCD (pQCD) calculations for the color-suppressed decays  
\[
B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta,\qquad B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'
\]
predict small branching fractions at the \(10^{-5}\) level, mainly controlled by the \(d\bar d\) component of the \(\eta^{(\prime)}\) wave functions and by the \(\eta-\eta'\) mixing scheme.

Typical pQCD estimates are approximately
\[
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0\to J/\psi\,\eta)\simeq 1.5\text{--}2.0\times 10^{-5},
\]
\[
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0\to J/\psi\,\eta')\simeq 0.8\text{--}1.2\times 10^{-5},
\]
with theoretical uncertainties from hadronic wave-function parameters, CKM inputs, scale dependence, and the \(\eta-\eta'\) mixing angle.

The predicted rate for \(B_d^0\to J/\psi\,\eta\) is broadly consistent with existing experimental measurements, which also lie around \(10^{-5}\). The \(J/\psi\,\eta'\) mode is expected to be somewhat smaller and remains experimentally more challenging, with present constraints not in significant tension with pQCD expectations.

These channels are relevant for future LHCb and high-luminosity LHC studies because improved measurements can test pQCD factorization in color-suppressed \(B\) decays, constrain \(\eta-\eta'\) mixing effects, and provide complementary information on hadronic uncertainties in \(B\to J/\psi P\) transitions.

We report a study of the color-suppressed decays \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\), motivated by the first experimental evidence for these modes and their relevance to \(SU(3)\)-flavor symmetry tests and \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing in nonleptonic \(B\)-meson decays. Using the measured branching fractions  
\[
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta)=
\left(1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}\right)\times 10^{-6},
\]
and  
\[
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta')=
\left(1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}\right)\times 10^{-6},
\]
we examine their consistency with expectations based on the related \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \pi^0\) and \(B_s^0 \to J/\psi \eta^{(\prime)}\) channels. The observed hierarchy and large uncertainties are compatible with a suppressed \(b\to c\bar c d\) transition and provide preliminary constraints on the singlet and octet components of the \(\eta^{(\prime)}\) wave functions. We discuss the implications for phenomenological descriptions of hadronic matrix elements, including factorization-based approaches and possible nonfactorizable contributions. Although the current precision does not yet permit a stringent determination of the \(\eta\)–\(\eta'\) mixing parameters, these measurements establish an important experimental input for global analyses of charmonium-assisted \(B\) decays and motivate improved studies at LHCb and Belle II.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.output:
We study the color-suppressed decays \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta^{(\prime)}\) within the perturbative QCD factorization framework based on transverse-momentum-dependent wave functions. The decay amplitudes are calculated including factorizable and nonfactorizable contributions, with particular attention to the role of spectator scattering and the interplay between the \(B\)-meson, charmonium, and \(\eta\)-\(\eta'\) distribution amplitudes. The \(\eta\)-\(\eta'\) system is treated in the quark-flavor mixing scheme, allowing the two branching ratios to be related directly to the light-quark and possible gluonic components of the final-state mesons.

We show that \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta^{(\prime)}\) decays provide a clean probe of QCD dynamics in color-suppressed \(b \to c\bar c d\) transitions. In particular, the predicted branching fractions are sensitive to the shape of the charmonium wave function, the size of nonfactorizable spectator contributions, Sudakov suppression effects, and the \(\eta\)-\(\eta'\) mixing parameters. Because the short-distance weak transition is well controlled, deviations between theory and experiment can be used to test the validity of perturbative factorization in heavy-to-light charmonium modes and to constrain poorly known hadronic inputs. We also discuss correlations with related channels such as \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \pi^0\) and \(B_s^0 \to J/\psi \eta^{(\prime)}\), emphasizing how ratios of branching fractions reduce theoretical uncertainties and sharpen sensitivity to the underlying QCD mechanisms.

Our results indicate that measurements of \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'\) at current and future flavor experiments can serve as useful tests of perturbative QCD descriptions of color-suppressed \(B\) decays and of the flavor structure of the \(\eta^{(\prime)}\) mesons.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

\textbf{Abstract}

We study the color-suppressed decays \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta\) and \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'\) in the perturbative QCD factorization approach. Both factorizable and nonfactorizable contributions are evaluated, including the effects of \(\eta-\eta'\) mixing in the quark-flavor basis. Using standard inputs for the \(B\)-meson and charmonium wave functions, CKM parameters, and decay constants, we obtain
\[
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta) \simeq 9.6 \times 10^{-6},
\qquad
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta') \simeq 5.4 \times 10^{-6},
\]
with theoretical uncertainties dominated by hadronic parameters and scale dependence. The predicted branching ratio for \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta\) is consistent with recent experimental measurements, supporting the applicability of the pQCD framework to these color-suppressed charmonium modes. The \(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'\) channel, expected at the level of a few \(10^{-6}\), should be accessible with larger data samples and can be further tested at the LHC, in particular by LHCb. Future measurements of both modes will provide useful constraints on \(\eta-\eta'\) mixing and on nonfactorizable dynamics in exclusive \(B\)-meson decays.
